notes:
v2.7.0 is about getting paid and keeping your records straight. Invoices go out the way customers expect, Bank Rec takes OFX files, keeps your receipts and picks the right invoice for a deposit, and bank rules can split a bill. Tablets for table service work properly over Wi-Fi, and this release closes security gaps in LAN mode.

New in v2.7.0:

Approve & Email sends an invoice straight to Sent once the email goes. If you close the email window without sending, it stays a draft. Save & Mark as Sent is gone from the editor: for an invoice you print or send another way, save it and use More → Mark as Sent.

Email an invoice to several people. To and CC take several addresses separated by commas, and Send me a copy puts a copy in your own inbox (sending from Dogbox doesn't put one in your Sent folder). The same goes for overdue notices and credit notes.

Customer Order No. A new field on the invoice for the customer's purchase order or reference. It prints on the invoice as "Your Order No", and the invoice list's search finds it.

Send an invoice's attachments with it. Timesheets or photos attached to an invoice are listed under Also attach in the email window; tick the ones to send with the PDF.

Pay several invoices at once: tick them in the Invoices list and click Record Payment. Ticking bills and clicking Pay Selected opens Payment Run with them chosen.

Bank Rec imports OFX files (.ofx, .qfx, .qbo) as well as CSV, with no column mapping.

Receipts on bank transactions. On a Bank Rec card, click Receipt and choose a photo or PDF, or drop the file on the card. When you click OK it moves onto the transaction. The Account transactions tab has a paperclip on each row to add receipts later, and a "Spent with no receipt" filter to find the ones missing.

Bank Rec picks the right invoice for a deposit more often: the one whose number is in the bank text, then the only one owing that amount, then the one whose customer's name is in the text. If two invoices owe the same amount and nothing tells them apart, neither is ticked, so you choose. One deposit can pay several invoices, and one payment several bills: tick each of them on the card.

Bank rules can set the GST code, and can split each matching line by percentage, such as a phone bill that's half business and half private. Split a card yourself and tick Remember to save the split as a rule. Rules also have a Contact field.

Contacts can be a Customer, Supplier, Employee or Contractor, using the new Is a buttons. In the visit form, + Add contractor adds a worker on the spot, and in Day view you can drag a visit into another worker's column.

Hourly tasks: + Log time records time against a task, and hourly tasks now go on task invoices.

Tablets for table service: a Full screen button hides the browser's address bar, and a tablet being used stays signed in instead of being sent back to sign-in after 10 minutes.

The user guides and in-app Help are updated for all of the above.

Bug fixes in v2.7.0:

Emailing an approved invoice marked it Sent, but the screen didn't update, so it looked unchanged until you reloaded.

Emailed PDFs had a jumble of letters in the file name. Invoices, quotes, bills and statements now arrive as INV-00005.pdf and so on.

Importing a bank CSV without a balance column skipped a second identical transaction on the same day.

Payment Run left out part-paid bills.

Hourly tasks were left off task invoices.

Editing a bank rule removed its contact.

A tablet could keep using an old copy of its screen after an update.

Security fixes in v2.7.0 (LAN mode):

Another device on the network could open, create or browse company files on the computer running Dogbox. Only that computer can now. A tablet that connects before the company is open waits, then carries on by itself.

A signed-in tablet or other computer could close Dogbox for everyone (the power icon), restart it, or make it install an update from any web address. These now only work on the computer running Dogbox, and other devices don't show the power icon.
